uncited: Level 1 Triangle-Voxel Classification maps a triangle mesh into a coarse 3D voxel grid by determining which voxels intersect with each triangle.
It solves the problem of spatial indexing for volume rendering by creating a list of candidate triangles for every voxel, enabling efficient downstream processing.

It differs from [Tessellation-based Voxelization](5430-tessellation-based-voxelization.md) by operating on a fixed grid rather than tessellating geometry, and from [Fake Voxelization via Triangle-Cube Intersection](6951-fake-voxelization-via-triangle-cube-intersection.md) by explicitly computing overlaps for all voxels in the triangle's bounding box rather than approximating with a single cube.
- Populated `voxelTriIndexCUDAData` and `voxelTriCountCUDAData` indicating which triangles intersect which voxels.
If overlap, compute linear index: $r \times \text{numDiv}.y \times \text{numDiv}.x + q \times \text{numDiv}.x + p$.
- **Time Complexity:** $O(N \cdot B)$, where $N$ is the number of triangles and $B$ is the average number of voxels in the triangle's bounding box.
The bounding box size depends on triangle size relative to voxel size.
- **Memory Complexity:** $O(V + T_{total})$, where $V$ is the number of voxels and $T_{total}$ is the total number of triangle-voxel intersections stored, capped by `triBufferLen` per voxel.
Performance scales with the number of triangles and the spatial coherence of the mesh.
- **Limitations:** Coarse resolution may miss thin features; requires careful handling of boundary conditions; memory usage can be high for dense meshes.
Originated in the GPView project by idealab-isu, this method is part of a pipeline for real-time volume rendering from mesh data.
It is designed for GPU execution, utilizing CUDA kernels for parallel processing.

- Vertices exactly on `objBoxMax` must be clamped to the last voxel index to prevent out-of-bounds access [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly shows the logic `if (boxNumX == numDiv.x && vertex.x == objBoxMax.x) boxNumX--;` (and similarly for Y and Z). This code ensures that if a vertex is exactly at `objBoxMax`, its calculated voxel index (which would be `numDiv`, an out-of-bounds index for a 0-based array of size `numDiv`) is decremented to `numDiv - 1` (the last valid voxel index). This prevents out-of-bounds access.
